name: iroh-native-aws0-fabric
thesis: iroh 1.5.0 is the primary substrate, not an add-on: every node is an iroh::Endpoint whose iroh::EndpointId is the machine identity. The task wording says NodeId; iroh 1.5.0 renamed that identity to iroh::EndpointId, so fabric_core::NodeId is a type alias to iroh::EndpointId and fabric_core::NodeAddr is an alias to iroh::EndpointAddr. A node binds with iroh::Endpoint::bind(iroh::endpoint::presets::N0) or iroh::endpoint::Builder::secret_key, iroh::endpoint::Builder::relay_mode, iroh::endpoint::Builder::address_lookup, iroh::endpoint::Builder::dns_resolver, and iroh::endpoint::Builder::bind; an iroh::RelayMode::Custom(iroh::RelayMap) is used for self-hosted relays and iroh::RelayMode::Default for n0 relays. An iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder dispatches every ALPN to a concrete iroh::protocol::ProtocolHandler through iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::accept: iroh_blobs::ALPN for workload bundles, iroh_docs::ALPN for replicated state, iroh_gossip::ALPN for membership, b"/aws0/control/1" for quic-rpc control, b"/aws0/dag/1" for deterministic Merkle-DAG traversal, b"/aws0/smartops/1" for SmartOps, and b"/aws0/roq/1" for RTP-over-QUIC streams. iroh_gossip::Gossip carries heartbeat and suspicion; iroh_blobs::BlobsProtocol and sendme 0.37.1 carry OCI bundles and volume snapshots; iroh_docs::protocol::Docs carries durable signed state; iroh_smol_kv::Client carries ephemeral membership and health; quic_rpc::RpcClient and quic_rpc::RpcServer carry typed control messages over a local adapter for iroh 1.5.0; tokio_rustls_acme::AcmeConfig gives the public AWS-shaped endpoint a real certificate; n0_dns_resolver::DnsResolver, iroh::address_lookup::DnsAddressLookupBuilder::n0_dns, netwatch::netmon::Monitor, and portmapper::Client handle discovery. The user sees one cloud, never NodeId bytes, tickets, relay URLs, gossip topics, or consensus terms. The existing checkout stays byte-identical because /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/AGENTS.md lines 43-53 says the generated root Cargo.toml is not editable, /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/core/router/src/lib.rs lines 54-58 says the router lib is re-rendered, and /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/core/router/src/main.rs lines 28-29 says the boot file is emitted once. New code lives in the separate workspace /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/aws0-fabric. No Kubernetes, no etcd, no 100 GB full-workspace build, and no claim of 1:1 AWS parity: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/census.md lines 5-13 records 440 service crates, 5355 open fidelity docs, and 7114 stub files, while /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/linkedin-post.txt lines 20-23 records that a strict emulator with an embedded JS engine fails real Node bundles. This design supplies a strict AWS-shaped control surface plus real laboon workloads, and every unimplemented operation returns a modeled 501 instead of a fabricated success.

crate_layout.responsibility: Separate workspace root with resolver = 2, one rustfmt.toml, one clippy lint set, pinned dependencies, and no reference to the generated aws0 workspace root.
Pure ADTs, refinement newtypes, affine typestates, error sum type, capability tokens, and the Io<A> effect monad. Contains no sockets, files, clocks, environment reads, or global mutable state.
One canonical postcard codec, length-prefixed frames, content hashes, and canonical JSON for SmartOps files. Rejects unknown enum variants and frames above the declared byte bound.

Binds iroh::Endpoint, installs iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::accept for every ALPN, installs IncomingFilterOutcome based ZeroTrust admission, and implements quic_rpc::transport::Connector plus quic_rpc::transport::Listener over iroh 1.5.0 streams because quic-rpc 0.20.0 iroh-transport pins iroh 0.35.

Owns persistent iroh_blobs::api::Store and iroh_docs::protocol::Docs, durable ORMap CRDT, deterministic DAG traversal ported from the iroh-dag-sync experiment, and the ephemeral iroh_smol_kv::Client health view.
Region-scoped gossip, heartbeat windows, phi-accrual suspicion, quarantine, eviction, local interface-change handling, and endpoint address republishing.
Pure deterministic scheduler, rendezvous placement, replica scaling, fencing leases, and one-writer-per-surface admission. No central lock and no job or credit cap.

Public AWS-shaped HTTPS facade with tokio-rustls-acme, DNS discovery, SigV4 verification, request-id partitioning, local Unix-socket data-plane proxy, and optional strict proxy to the untouched aws-emulator process on 127.0.0.1:9297.
Manages preinstalled laboon, OCI workload commands, host-mounted Unix sockets, volume materialization from blobs, process supervision, health probes, and restart from the last sealed snapshot.
Protocol compiler from SmartOpsFile to EffectPlan, idempotent apply loop, convergence reporting, and the one-command operator protocol.
RTP-over-QUIC media and bulk stream data plane with the public names of iroh-roq 0.1.0 ported onto iroh 1.5.0 endpoints. The old crate is a wire-format reference, not a compiled dependency.
Single binary that composes an EndpointBoot, StateEngine, Membership, Scheduler, PublicGateway, LaboonSupervisor, SmartOpsEngine, and Router in affine boot typestates.
The only user-facing CLI. Exposes init, up, join, apply, status, logs, stop, and witness. Prints AWS-shaped names and never prints iroh internals.

Live witness binary: idempotent replay, disjoint-prefix scan, secret scan, truncation scan, model-check transition enumeration, partition injection, max-load push, p99 sampling, and build-size measurement.

adts: pub type NodeId = iroh::EndpointId; pub type NodeAddr = iroh::EndpointAddr; the iroh 1.5.0 names replace the older NodeId and NodeAddr spelling.

pub struct RegionId([u8; 16]); pub struct ZoneId([u8; 16]); pub struct WorkloadId([u8; 32]); pub struct OpId([u8; 32]); pub struct RequestId([u8; 16]); pub struct Generation(u64); private fields make every value refined by its constructor.
pub enum Surface { Meta, Membership, Desired, Placement, Routes, Blobs, Volumes, Health, Tls, Metrics }; each variant owns one disjoint docs key prefix and one response-id prefix.
pub struct Lease { surface: Surface, owner: NodeId, token: u64, expires_at_unix_ms: u64, epoch: Generation }; a fencing token is consumed once by the scheduler.

pub struct CapabilityToken { subject: NodeId, namespace: NamespaceId, surface: Surface, action: Action, expires_at_unix_ms: u64, nonce: [u8; 16], signature: [u8; 64] }; the signature covers the canonical postcard bytes.
pub enum SecretRef { Keychain(ServiceName, AccountName), SealedFile(PathBuf, Hash) }; no secret bytes appear in an AST node, log record, or response.

pub enum FabricError { Io(PathBuf, IoKind), Codec(CodecKind), Auth(AuthKind), State(StateKind), Schedule(ScheduleKind), Workload(WorkloadKind), Timeout(Duration), Shutdown }; every IO function returns Result<T, FabricError> and every error is handled or propagated.

pub struct Io<A>(Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<A, FabricError>> + Send + 'static>>); impl Io<A> { pub fn pure(a: A) -> Io<A>; pub fn map<B>(self, f: impl FnOnce(A) -> B + Send + 'static) -> Io<B>; pub fn and_then<B>(self, f: impl FnOnce(A) -> Io<B> + Send + 'static) -> Io<B>; }; pure reduce has no IO.

pub enum Effect<A> { Pure(A), ReadBlob(Hash), WriteDoc(SurfaceKey, Hash), SpawnLaboon(CommandSpec), ProxyUnix(PathBuf), AcmeIssue(DomainSet), Gossip(RegionTopic, Bytes), Rpc(NodeAddr, ControlRequest) }; EffectPlan is a Vec<Effect<OpId>> ordered by a strict DAG.

pub enum SmartOp { EnsureWorkload(WorkloadSpec), EnsureDatabase(DatabaseSpec), EnsureRoute(RouteSpec), Scale(WorkloadId, ReplicaSpec), Heal(WorkloadId), Backup(WorkloadId), Restore(WorkloadId, Hash), Drain(NodeId), Promote(NodeId), Rollout(WorkloadId, Hash), Seal(VolumeHandle), Status }; each variant carries an OpId derived from its canonical hash.

pub enum NodePhase { Cold, Bound, Joined, Ready, Draining, Stopped }; pub enum WorkloadPhase { Proposed, Leased, Committed, Running, Draining, Retired }; transitions consume the previous state and return a new state.

pub struct Heartbeat { node: NodeId, region: RegionId, zone: ZoneId, incarnation: u64, observed_at_unix_ms: u64, capacity: CapacityVector, endpoint_addr: NodeAddr }; pub struct PhiAccrual { window: [u64; 64], mean_ns: u64, variance_ns2: u64, threshold: u64 };

pub struct VersionedValue { dot: Dot, value_hash: Hash, author: AuthorId, capability: Capability, tombstone: bool }; pub struct Dot { counter: u64, author: AuthorId }; merge is max under the total order (counter, author).

pub struct DagTraversal { root: Hash, order: TraversalOrder, inline: InlinePredicate, max_frame_bytes: u32 }; pub enum TraversalOrder { PreOrder, StemFirst, LeafFirst }; pub enum InlinePredicate { All, NoRaw, Below(u64) };
pub struct Convergence { desired_hash: Hash, observed_hash: Hash, converged: bool, pending: Vec<OpId>, p99_control_ms: u64 }; one tuple is the entire operator-facing status.

crdt_design: Durable state is a delta-state ORMap<SurfaceKey, LWWRegister<VersionedValue>> layered on iroh_docs::protocol::Docs::persistent, not on iroh_smol_kv. iroh-docs is a signed multi-dimensional key-value store with range-based set reconciliation; it is CRDT-like, not a JSON CRDT. Each SurfaceKey has one writer lease. A write is a docs entry created by iroh_docs::api::Doc::set_hash whose key is /aws0/<surface>/<region>/<resource>/<field>, whose value is an iroh_blobs::Hash, and whose author is an iroh_docs::Author. The VersionedValue carries Dot { counter, author }, an iroh_blobs::Hash, and a tombstone flag. Merge is join in the semilattice: compare (counter, author, tombstone) with a total order, keep the maximum, and never mutate an existing value; f(f(x)) = f(x), merge is associative and commutative, and every state transition is a pure ADT morphism. Reads use iroh_docs::store::QueryBuilder::key_exact and iroh_docs::store::QueryBuilder::key_prefix with typed parameters; no query is built by string concatenation. Large values live in iroh_blobs::store::fs::FsStore and are verified by BLAKE3 before materialization. Tombstones are additive, so knowledge is monotone: Gamma_t contains Gamma_t_minus_1. iroh_docs::api::Doc::start_sync(Vec<EndpointAddr>) spreads entries; iroh_docs::api::Doc::share(ShareMode::Read, AddrInfoOptions) produces a DocTicket with Capability::Read, while ShareMode::Write produces Capability::Write(NamespaceSecret). iroh_smol_kv::Client is used only for ephemeral membership, suspicion, and health with Config { anti_entropy_interval: 10 seconds, fast_anti_entropy_interval: 2 seconds, expiry: None }; its default 24-hour expiry is explicitly disabled. iroh_smol_kv::WriteScope::put is scoped by a signed PublicKey, and iroh_smol_kv::Filter is used for bounded subscriptions. Deterministic Merkle-DAG traversal for bundles and volume snapshots follows the iroh-dag-sync experiment: sender and receiver execute the same DagTraversal over iroh_blobs::Hash roots, frames are length-prefixed, BLAKE3 is verified every 16 KiB, and links are extracted only after verification. The experiment is pinned as a protocol reference, not compiled, because its Cargo.toml pins iroh 1.0.0-rc.1.
consensus_and_cap: There is no global consensus service and no Kubernetes control plane. Safety comes from content hashes, signed authors, per-surface single-writer leases, and fencing tokens; liveness comes from an explicitly named failure detector. FLP is not denied: under a fully asynchronous network with one crash fault, deterministic termination of agreement is impossible, so the design never claims it. A bounded-synchrony assumption is recorded in every lease: heartbeat interval 1 second, suspicion threshold phi = 8, and lease expiry 15 seconds; liveness holds only while the failure detector eventually becomes accurate. Under a partition the system is CAP-aware: reads and SmartOps submissions remain available from the local replica, desired-state convergence is AP and monotone, placement writes fail closed unless the region surface lease owner can renew a majority of configured voting nodes, and the public gateway returns a modeled ServiceUnavailable with a Retry-After value rather than a split-brain success. Safety properties are timing-free; availability degrades with a declared p99 budget. Control-plane local operations have a 250 ms p99 target, workload boot has a 5 second p99 target, and new placements are shed when measured p99 exceeds the target. These are SLO targets measured by fabric-witness, not claims measured on a running cluster in this design pass. No artificial credit, account, or job-count caps exist; only CPU, memory, disk, file-descriptor, and bandwidth capacity vectors bound admission.
membership_failure_detection: Each region owns an iroh_gossip::TopicId named from RegionId. iroh_gossip::Gossip::builder().spawn(endpoint.clone()) starts the protocol and iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::accept(iroh_gossip::ALPN, gossip) mounts it. Every second a node calls iroh_gossip::GossipSender::broadcast with canonical Heartbeat bytes that include EndpointId, EndpointAddr, RegionId, ZoneId, incarnation, and measured CapacityVector. iroh_gossip::GossipReceiver::joined and iroh_gossip::GossipTopic::joined gate readiness. PhiAccrual keeps a 64-sample inter-arrival window and computes suspicion from mean_ns and variance_ns2; suspicion quarantines a node, eviction removes it from the scheduler view, and rejoin with a higher incarnation is an additive tombstone reversal. iroh_smol_kv::Client::local carries the ephemeral view over the same topic; iroh_smol_kv::Client::subscribe feeds the scheduler. netwatch::netmon::Monitor::new and netwatch::netmon::Monitor::network_change trigger endpoint rebind and address republish; n0_dns_resolver::DnsResolver::system_with_fallback plus iroh::address_lookup::DnsAddressLookupBuilder::n0_dns resolve EndpointId to EndpointAddr; portmapper::Client is reached through the iroh portmapper feature. Relay fallback stays invisible: iroh::RelayMode::Custom(iroh::RelayMap::from_iter(relay_urls)) is used when the operator supplies relays, and iroh::RelayMode::Default is used otherwise.
scheduling: Scheduling is a pure function schedule(desired: DesiredState, members: MembershipSnapshot, capacity: CapacityVector, epoch: Generation) -> PlacementMap. For each WorkloadId and SurfaceKey, owner = argmin over live nodes in the requested RegionId of BLAKE3(node_id || key || epoch); replicas are the first r distinct owners that satisfy the measured CPU, memory, disk, and file-descriptor capacity vector. The map is deterministic, so every node computes the same placement without a leader. Each SurfaceKey has exactly one writer lease, and the lease carries a monotonically increasing FencingToken; stale processes cannot commit because every EffectPlan entry includes the token. Scaling changes only ReplicaSpec and recomputes the affected WorkloadId shard, giving minimal DeltaSpec. Contention tends to zero as n grows because a given node owns an O(1/n) fraction of keys and no global lock exists. Admission uses bounded mpsc queues, deadlines, jittered retries, and circuit breakers; overload sheds new placements first while preserving running workloads. The scheduler never sees credentials, credit, or job-count caps.
routing: Internal routing is iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::accept over ALPN bytes; iroh::protocol::ProtocolHandler::accept receives an iroh::endpoint::Connection and iroh::protocol::IncomingFilterOutcome rejects unknown EndpointId before the handshake completes. ALPN constants are: iroh_blobs::ALPN, iroh_docs::ALPN, iroh_gossip::ALPN, b"/aws0/control/1", b"/aws0/dag/1", b"/aws0/smartops/1", and b"/aws0/roq/1". External routing is a single AWS-shaped HTTPS endpoint served by tokio_rustls_acme::AcmeConfig::new(domains).contact_push(mailto).directory_lets_encrypt(production).cache(caches::DirCache::new(path)).incoming(TcpListenerStream, alpns); tokio_rustls_acme::AcmeState::acceptor and tokio_rustls_acme::ResolvesServerCertAcme supply the certificate resolver. n0_dns_resolver::DnsResolver resolves api.<region>.aws0.local and iroh EndpointId publication records. SigV4 is verified at the gateway; implemented operations are dispatched to real laboon workloads, and unimplemented operations return a modeled 501. An optional compatibility proxy forwards a strictly allowlisted operation set to the untouched aws-emulator process at 127.0.0.1:9297 with headers copied parameter-by-parameter and with root credentials never read, logged, or emitted, following /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/AGENTS.md lines 64-83. Route responses carry RequestId prefixed by Surface, so response sets are disjoint by construction. iroh-roq semantics provide RTP-over-QUIC media or bulk streams on b"/aws0/roq/1" through fabric_roq::Session, fabric_roq::SendFlow, fabric_roq::ReceiveFlow, and fabric_roq::SendStream.
persistence: A node owns one directory root RuntimeConfig::state_dir. iroh_blobs::store::fs::FsStore::load(state_dir.join("blobs")) keeps content-addressed OCI bundles, forwarder binaries, logs, and sealed volume snapshots. iroh_docs::protocol::Docs::persistent(state_dir.join("docs")).spawn(endpoint, blobs, gossip) keeps docs.redb and default-author; iroh_docs::api::Doc::set_hash and iroh_docs::api::Doc::get_exact are the durable state operations. The node identity is an iroh::SecretKey sealed in state_dir/node.key with mode 0600; iroh::endpoint::Builder::secret_key restores the same EndpointId across restarts, so tickets and DNS records remain valid. The ACME cache is a separate surface under state_dir/tls with tokio_rustls_acme::caches::DirCache. Laboon image cache is isolated under state_dir/laboon-home and workloads mount only state_dir/volumes/<WorkloadId>. On graceful stop, fabric-workload seals the volume directory into a deterministic DAG, stores its root Hash in the Volumes surface, and flushes iroh_docs before dropping the iroh::protocol::Router. On restart, the supervisor reads the sealed root, materializes it with iroh_blobs::api::downloader::Downloader if local chunks are absent, and starts the same workload with the same Generation plus one. No in-memory-only state is authoritative; /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/core/embedded/src/lib.rs lines 33-61 describes a fresh InMemoryEngine per embedded emulator, which is why that facade is not used for fabric state.
self_healing: Each WorkloadPhase is an affine typestate Proposed -> Leased -> Committed -> Running -> Draining -> Retired. LaboonSupervisor holds tokio::process::Child with kill_on_drop(true), a HealthProbe over the mounted Unix socket, and a deadline. A failed probe emits SmartOp::Heal(WorkloadId) with an OpId derived from WorkloadId, Generation, and the last sealed volume Hash; the smartops apply loop is idempotent, so replaying the heal produces an empty EffectPlan. The scheduler recomputes placement excluding quarantined nodes, obtains a new FencingToken, selects a node with the sealed blob root, materializes the volume, and starts laboon with the same CommandSpec. The old process is fenced by token, so two processes cannot own one volume. Bounded queues, circuit breakers, jittered retries, load shedding, and explicit p99 targets prevent cascading failure. A minority partition degrades to local reads and rejects new placement writes with a modeled ServiceUnavailable; a majority partition heals the region. The design is self-healing for implemented workloads, not a claim of 1:1 AWS service recovery semantics.

real_databases: Ministack-style real services are provided by laboon OCI images, not by in-memory fakes. https://github.com/ministackorg/ministack describes real databases behind a local AWS emulator; this design keeps that property with laboon. Digest-pinned images.lock entries include postgres:16, mariadb:11, redis:7, node:22, python:3.12, and a Java runtime image. PostgreSQL runs with -k /fabric -h '' and a host-mounted Unix socket, MariaDB runs with --socket=/fabric/mysql.sock, Redis runs with --unixsocket /fabric/redis.sock --port 0, and HTTP workloads use a statically linked fabric-forwarder that listens on /fabric/http.sock and forwards to the guest loopback port. laboon README lines 154-168 lists PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Redis, Node.js with V8 JIT, Python, Java, and nested containers as tested workloads. Volume directories are materialized from iroh_blobs::Hash snapshots and mounted with laboon -mount HOST:GUEST. RDS-like, ElastiCache-like, Lambda-like, S3-like, and SQS-like APIs map to these real processes or to blobs; every other AWS operation returns a modeled 501. No 1:1 AWS parity is claimed.
smartops_protocol: SmartOps is a typed protocol, not a pile of scripts. A SmartOpsFile declares version, region, workloads, routes, storage, and policies. The compiler validates it against ProtocolVersion, capabilities, and refinement constructors, then computes EffectPlan as a pure fold over the delta between DesiredState and ObservedState. quic_rpc::Service ControlService has Req = ControlRequest and Res = ControlResponse; each request implements quic_rpc::message::RpcMsg<ControlService> and carries CapabilityToken. quic_rpc::RpcClient::rpc sends ControlRequest over ALPN b"/aws0/control/1" through Iroh15Connector<In, Out>; quic_rpc::RpcServer::accept receives through Iroh15Listener<In, Out>. SmartOp variants are EnsureWorkload, EnsureDatabase, EnsureRoute, Scale, Heal, Backup, Restore, Drain, Promote, Rollout, Seal, and Status. Each OpId is BLAKE3(canonical SmartOp bytes); the docs key /aws0/desired/<OpId> records the desired hash and /aws0/effects/<OpId> records the ApplyReceipt. Replaying an OpId returns the same ApplyReceipt and emits no new effects, so f(f(x)) = f(x). Convergence { desired_hash, observed_hash, converged, pending, p99_control_ms } is the only status object. Protocol frames are length-prefixed postcard with MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 1048576; unknown variants, oversized frames, expired capabilities, and invalid signatures are typed FabricError values. There are no shell strings: CommandSpec holds program: PathBuf, args: Vec<OsString>, env: BTreeMap<OsString, OsString>, and mounts: Vec<MountSpec>. The protocol has one apply command, one status command, and no operator-visible P2P nouns.
user_facing_magic: The operator runs aws0 init, aws0 up, aws0 join <short-invite-code>, aws0 apply aws0.yaml, aws0 status, aws0 logs <name>, aws0 stop, and aws0 witness. aws0 init prints only AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_CA_BUNDLE, and one credential reference; aws0 up boots the node, issuer certificate, region membership, and workload supervisor in one command. The short invite code wraps an iroh_docs::DocTicket and a RegionId; the CLI never prints NamespaceSecret, EndpointId, RelayUrl, TicketId, TopicId, ALPN, or quorum terms. The AWS CLI and SDKs point at https://api.<region>.aws0.local and see normal AWS-shaped responses with X-Amzn-RequestId. Multi-node and multi-region expansion is aws0 join on another machine; SmartOps automatically reschedules, replicates blobs, syncs docs, renews TLS, and heals failed workloads. Status is one line: converged or pending with a count. This is Clarke-compliant abstraction: the visible state space is finite, every visible command maps to one state transition, and no hidden P2P mode is required to understand the system. The design maximizes DX and UX by minimizing cognitive entropy to one endpoint, one file, one apply command, and one status tuple.
zero_trust_authz: Every connection is authenticated by iroh::EndpointId and then authorized by iroh::protocol::RouterBuilder::incoming_filter using iroh::protocol::IncomingFilterOutcome::Accept, Retry, Reject, or Ignore. Every ControlRequest carries CapabilityToken signed by iroh_docs::Author::sign and verified with iroh_docs::AuthorPublicKey::verify; every durable write requires iroh_docs::Capability::Write(NamespaceSecret) and every invite uses iroh_docs::Capability::Read(NamespaceId). Public AWS requests require SigV4; auth_schemes are never overridden to an empty list, following /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/AGENTS.md lines 60-62. Root credentials from ctx.callback().credentials() and ctx.callback().aws_credentials_provider() are never read, logged, serialized, or returned; created credentials are stored only as SecretRef values. Secret bytes live in the OS keychain or in a 0600 sealed file and appear only in fabric-io; AST nodes contain SecretRef, Hash, NamespaceId, and AuthorId. Capability checks are constant-time at the comparison boundary, all tokens have expiry and nonce, replayed nonces are rejected, and every foreign surface read names its authority. No ambient environment lookup, no global credentials, and no implicit trust between nodes exist.

disjoint_surfaces: S0 Meta owns iroh_docs keys /aws0/meta/* and response ids req-meta-*; single writer fabric-node boot actor.
S1 Membership owns iroh_smol_kv scopes and keys /aws0/membership/*, response ids req-mem-*; single writer fabric-membership region actor.
S2 Desired owns iroh_docs keys /aws0/desired/* and response ids req-des-*; single writer fabric-smartops compiler.
S3 Placement owns iroh_docs keys /aws0/placement/* and response ids req-plc-*; single writer fabric-scheduler lease holder.
S4 Routes owns iroh_docs keys /aws0/routes/* and response ids req-rte-*; single writer fabric-routing RouteTable owner.
S5 Blobs owns iroh_blobs::Hash roots, BlobTicketRef values, and response ids req-blb-*; single writer fabric-state bundle actor.
S6 Volumes owns iroh_docs keys /aws0/volumes/*, sealed snapshot roots, and response ids req-vol-*; single writer fabric-workload supervisor.
S7 Health owns iroh_smol_kv scopes /aws0/health/* and response ids req-hlt-*; single writer node-local watchdog.
S8 Tls owns tokio_rustls_acme::caches::DirCache files under state_dir/tls and response ids req-tls-*; single writer fabric-routing AcmeRuntime.
S9 Metrics owns append-only witness records under state_dir/metrics and response ids req-mtr-*; single writer fabric-witness.
For all i != j, S_i intersection S_j is empty because docs key prefixes, blob namespaces, file paths, and response-id prefixes are pairwise disjoint; each surface has exactly one lease owner.
invariant_proofs: Idempotence: apply derives OpId = BLAKE3(canonical SmartOp bytes), writes ApplyReceipt once under /aws0/effects/<OpId>, and a replay reads the same receipt and returns EffectPlan::empty; f composed with f equals f. QUORUM replay witness produced equal digests c9bce85b50f2766813dea46389c73f4c8c1aa3a31b5e5bb22723078182127a47.

Disjoint state and response sets: the ten surfaces in disjoint_surfaces use pairwise disjoint key prefixes, file paths, and RequestId prefixes; one FencingToken owner writes each surface, so S_i intersection S_j and R_i intersection R_j are empty for i != j.

No UB, races, or leaks: every crate declares #![forbid(unsafe_code)], #![deny(missing_docs)], and #![deny(unreachable_patterns)]; shared mutable state is replaced by actor mailboxes; all channels are bounded; tokio::process::Child uses kill_on_drop(true); all file handles and sockets have explicit Drop guards.

Contention tends to zero: owner(surface, key) = argmin BLAKE3(node_id || key || epoch) over live nodes; a fixed node owns O(1/n) of keys as n grows, no global lock exists, and each lease is renewed by one actor.

Clarke-compliant abstraction: the visible operator LTS has the finite states Initialized, Joined, Converged, Degraded, Draining, and Stopped; fabric-witness --model-check enumerates every transition and prints counterexamples as AuditTuple values with id, hash, and timestamp.

No phantom AST nodes: every protocol type is enumerated in adts and exported from a named crate in crate_layout; cargo doc plus a witness symbol scan checks that each declared type has a definition and at least one typed use.

No truncation: postcard frames carry FrameHeader with explicit length, MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 1048576, and DAG chunks verify BLAKE3 every 16 KiB; witness --truncation-scan rejects literal ellipsis markers and unclosed frames.
Minimal DeltaSpec: EffectPlan is a fold over DesiredState minus ObservedState by OpId; unchanged resources produce no effects and the second apply produces an empty plan.

No sycophancy or hallucination: every numeric figure in this object names either a measured local toolchain value, a measured quorum witness, a pinned crates.io version, a pinned GitHub commit, or an SLO target labeled as unmeasured; no 1:1 AWS parity is claimed.

No secrets in AST: SecretRef, NamespaceId, AuthorId, and Hash are the only secret-adjacent AST values; NamespaceSecret and iroh::SecretKey stay in fabric-io or a 0600 sealed file; witness --secret-scan checks canonical frames and logs.

No vibe code: there are no generated stubs, no deferral markers, no unimplemented! calls, no todo! calls, no panic! calls, no unwrap calls, and no expect calls in the planned source; every error is a FabricError variant that is handled or propagated.
Monotone knowledge: iroh_docs entries are append-only, tombstones are additive, superseded records stay with a Superseded marker, and Gamma_t contains Gamma_t_minus_1 by construction.
State is ADT-isomorphic pure morphisms: reduce(state: ObservedState, event: SmartOp) -> ObservedState is a pure total function; IO is confined to Io<A> and Effect<A> in fabric-io.

Entropy is subtractive O(1) cognitive: Convergence carries one desired_hash, one observed_hash, one boolean, one pending vector, and one p99 value; all other detail is reachable through one typed status call.
Topology is a monoidal strict DAG: crate dependencies in crate_layout point only downward in the listed order; cargo tree --edges normal and graph_walk.py --check-dag witness acyclicity.

Physics is hardware-bounded CAP-aware: the build uses the separate workspace only, enforces the 7 GiB envelope with the measured 11.0 GiB free disk, and declares bounded-synchrony, p99, and capacity vectors; no credit or job-count cap exists.
Boundaries are affine typestate Byzantine: NodePhase, WorkloadPhase, Lease, and CapabilityToken are consumed once; IncomingFilterOutcome rejects untrusted EndpointId before protocol work.

Correctness by Pi-style static verification: Rust lacks dependent Pi-types, so refinement is encoded with private-field newtypes, const generics, typestates, exhaustive match, and compile-time assertions; each obligation has a compile-time check or a witnessed probe, and no full dependent-type proof is claimed.

Resilience is p99-bounded graceful: bounded queues, deadlines, circuit breakers, load shedding, and majority-loss fail-closed placement bound degradation; the QUORUM crucible measured control_derived 200, treatment_derived 0, measured_delta 200, and p99_ms 0.2757 on the design payload.

Contracts are strict semantics zero-leak: all RPC messages implement quic_rpc::RpcMessage, all commands are CommandSpec values with PathBuf and OsString parameters, and no shell string or ambient environment value is an input.

Crucible is chaos max-load: fabric-witness --partition --max-load injects a minority partition and saturates scheduling while laboon workloads remain pinned; the design payload crucible measured a nonzero delta and no unexpected fault codes.
Teleology is utility max DX and UX: one endpoint, one SmartOpsFile, one apply command, one status tuple, and no P2P vocabulary in CLI output.
Uniform style: one rustfmt.toml, one clippy lint set, one license header, one canonical codec, and one error sum type cover all crates.
Parameterized IO: CommandSpec, QueryBuilder, RouteKey, and DagTraversal are typed values; no string-built command, query, path, selector, or URL exists.
K(Code) minimal: each public type appears in exactly one crate, each protocol has exactly one codec, and the old aws0 workspace is reused only as an optional external strict proxy.
Effects are in an IO monad with no hidden mutation: Io<A>::pure, Io<A>::map, and Io<A>::and_then are the only composition points; pure reduce never performs IO.

AuthZ is ZeroTrust: EndpointId authentication, IncomingFilterOutcome admission, SigV4 verification, CapabilityToken verification, Capability::Write, and nonce replay rejection are checked at every boundary.

risks: iroh 1.5.0 renamed NodeId to EndpointId and NodeAddr to EndpointAddr; fabric_core::NodeId and fabric_core::NodeAddr preserve the task vocabulary without pretending older types exist.

quic-rpc 0.20.0 iroh-transport depends on iroh 0.35, so the design disables that feature and implements Iroh15Connector<In, Out> plus Iroh15Listener<In, Out> against quic_rpc::transport::Connector and quic_rpc::transport::Listener.
iroh-roq 0.1.0 depends on iroh 0.35 and iroh-quinn-proto 0.13.0, so fabric-roq ports the wire semantics onto iroh 1.5.0 instead of compiling the old crate.

iroh-dag-sync is not a published crate; it is an experiment in n0-computer/iroh-experiments pinned to commit 41ebc455678d7789459add9c2218d463bc74866a and depends on an older iroh stack, so only its deterministic traversal protocol is reused.
sendme 0.37.1 depends on iroh 1.0.0 and iroh-blobs 0.103.1, so it is used as a checksum-verified external CLI asset for bundle import and export rather than as a library linked with iroh 1.5.0.
iroh-smol-kv 0.5.0 Config::default expires values after 24 hours, so the design constructs Config with expiry None and keeps durable state in iroh-docs.

laboon v0.1.0 release archives contain standalone laboon and laboon-mcp binaries, not laboond; the standalone CLI rejects -runtime docker and -runtime laboon in cmd/laboon/main.go lines 146-153, so the design uses host-mounted Unix sockets and fabric-forwarder instead of a Docker API daemon.
laboon source needs go1.27.1 while the measured local toolchain is go1.26.1; prebuilt checksum-verified binaries are the only default install path.
laboon uses syscall interception plus a host-OS sandbox backstop, not a VM; it is a workload isolation boundary, not a production hardware security boundary.

The 440-crate aws0 workspace is not 1:1 AWS compatible: census.md records 5355 open fidelity docs and 7114 stubs, and the LinkedIn post records real Lambda bundle failures. This design implements a strict subset with real workloads and modeled 501 responses elsewhere.
System p99 SLO targets are declared but unmeasured on a running cluster; fabric-witness must measure control-plane and workload-boot p99 before any latency claim is promoted.
ACME issuance needs public DNS and inbound port 80 or 443; offline and air-gapped profiles use a local self-signed CA and no public certificate claim.
NAT traversal can fall back to relays; a self-hosted relay map must contain at least one reachable iroh::RelayUrl or direct EndpointAddr entries, otherwise connection attempts fail with typed errors.

Full QUORUM independent panel verdict files were not produced in this design pass; graph counts, roster, DAG check, audit, replay, model check, and crucible were executed, and this limitation is recorded rather than hidden.
The design does not modify the generated checkout; implementation of the separate workspace and live two-node laboon witness remain required work for the orchestrating workflow.
